title: Equipment & trading
summary: Custom qualities, heroic stats, bags and the trading economy.
body:
Browse the equipment catalog → Find a reward by slot, required level or source zone, with all four qualities grouped together.

Player trading and duplicate items

Trade formerly NO DROP and NO TRANSFER items, already-attuned gear, bags, their contents and augments. LORE restrictions are disabled, so duplicate ownership is allowed. Inventory capacity, temporary-item expiration and Pet Armor restrictions remain. Equipment eligibility still depends on your held classes and the remaining item requirements.

Polished, Exalted, and Ascended loot

Eligible dropped equipment and bags can appear in three stronger custom tiers. Their health, mana, defenses, and offensive stats scale by item family.

Prepared tuning, awaiting activation: ordinary eligible equipment and bags will roll 20% Polished, 5% Exalted and 1% Ascended per item drop, leaving 74% Normal. These are not chances per kill. Zone-hunt and dungeon rewards use their own rates.

New augments and gear in 48 Classic zones

Each eligible native enemy has a separate 0.5% chance for its zone’s augment and 0.5% chance for its new gear piece. Both can drop together, and ordinary loot remains. Each family averages one drop per 200 eligible kills; there is no guaranteed drop or pity counter. Once a family drops, its quality is Base 60%, Polished 30%, Exalted 8%, or Ascension 2%. Cities, hubs, pets, merchants and summoned copies do not provide these rewards. See the zone reward list.

Six armor locations for heroic augments

Eligible Base and tiered head, arms, hands, chest, legs and feet armor gains one type-22 socket, preserving existing sockets. Zone augments add stats and heroic attributes; item level requirements still apply. At level 50, every two effective heroic INT from these socketed augments allows one more point of item Spell Damage, up to +30; heroic WIS does the same for Healing Amount. With the current 250 cap, either can reach 280. Extra cap room only helps when you have enough of the actual bonus.

Upgrade matching rewards

#zoneforge uses three Base copies for one Polished reward, then four Polished for one Exalted or four Exalted for one Ascension. Artisan Veyra’s reusable Reforging Box also upgrades four identical Polished or Exalted copies, including eligible ordinary tiered gear. The box also accepts three identical eligible Normal/Base copies for Polished; higher recipes stay at four. Read Item upgrades for inputs, restrictions and the two distinct top-tier names.

Heroic stats on Ascended equipment

Ascended gear and Ascended epics add heroic stats on top of their improved base stats. This describes the existing equipment tiers; the new zone rewards have their own heroic stats at each quality.

Gear bonuses for casters and healers

Item Spell Damage and Heal Amount work as percentage bonuses, including damage-over-time and healing-over-time spells. The base cap for each item-bonus total is 250. Eligible zone augments can raise it to 280 at level 50 when enough actual bonus is equipped. Corrections to some existing tiered items are still in the works.

More room for core stats

The normal core-stat cap is raised to 425, with heroic stat effects handled separately.

Ascended summoned equipment

Eligible summoned gear becomes Ascended when a matching version exists. The supported Paladin and Cleric summoned-hammer families have zero merchant resale value at every quality, including items you already own. Summoning does not bypass spell or item-level requirements.

More room in your bags

Buy bags up to 40 slots, with base prices from 10 to 7,500 platinum. Merchant price adjustments and each bag’s capacity and contents restrictions still apply. Free trading does not reduce expensive bag purchase prices.

Better payouts for ordinary loot

Boosted merchant payouts remain in place for ordinary loot. Formerly NO DROP items use the fixed one-platinum payout below instead of those price modifiers.

One platinum for formerly NO DROP items

Ordinary merchants and #sellall pay exactly 1 platinum per physical item from the eligible formerly NO DROP pool. Five stack units pay 5 platinum; a charged object pays 1 platinum total. Purchase prices have a one-platinum floor. Merchant previews can differ from actual payment. Zone-hunt rewards, dungeon rewards and the supported divine summoned-hammer families have no merchant resale value.

Bulk selling from the command or merchant window

Use #sellall to sell eligible carried items without targeting a merchant, or use the merchant window’s Sell All button. Containers, food, drink, spell reagents and casting focus items are kept. Zero-value items, including zone rewards and the supported divine summoned hammers, are skipped. Sales are immediate and can include valuable gear. Bank anything you want to keep first.

Winged Helm of the Dawn

A custom Paladin helmet with an installed appearance for visual testing. No acquisition quest or loot source has been added yet.

Wear gear for your whole build

Ordinary equipment recognizes all held classes. Class-matching wearable items and augments allow all playable races; deity, level, slot, weapon and augment restrictions remain. See equipment eligibility.

Dungeon completion rewards

Raid and Grind dungeons have 24 shared reward designs and three exclusive Raid designs per dungeon. Grind grants Normal; Raid grants Polished or Ascended. These permanent, tradeable, non-lore items have zero merchant resale and no existing forging recipe. Their bags have up to ten slots and 100% weight reduction.
